newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SERIE A REVEALS ITS VITAL STATISTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SERIE A REVEALS ITS VITAL STATISTICS.

text.p: The last serie A season saw more goals scored, more actual time played and the highest number of penalties awarded in European soccer, Italy's refereeing supremo revealed on Wednesday.
Paolo Casarin announced the game's vital statistics and voiced concern about the penalties.
He told the serie A referees' end of season gathering near Florence that a total of 109 were conceded.
Of these 80 were indisputable, 10 were clearly "invented" and the remaining 19 were debatable.
But he said these goals were not the problem.

"The problem is not penalties granted because we are more or less in agreement in judging them. The problem arises when we find that according to commentators we should have awarded another 80, reaching the stratospheric number 189."
Casarin said he had nonetheless looked into these 80 alleged penalties and had decided that only 10 stood up.
He gave some other fascinating facts:
-- When he started in his job in 1990, 702 goals scored in Serie A. The latest tally was 808.
-- The ball was in play an average 60 minutes a match.
-- There was an average of 40 fouls a game.
He said this last figure was stable and within the European norm, although less than the Champions' League final with 55.
-- Throw-ins were up, with an average of 43.
-- The average number of bookings was 4.6 per match while there was a record total of 126 red cards.

Casarin said the number of sendings-off should have been even higher. "There were a lot of players who deserved a sending-off who, instead, stayed on the pitch and a few who were forced to leave because of an error by the referee."
